sections.label: Growth Sectors Initiative placements
sections.summary: MOM's Growth Sectors Initiative reskills locals through Professional Conversion Programmes, placing over 10,000 mid-career locals into PMET jobs in growth sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Under the Growth Sectors Initiative that we started in 2017, MOM works closely with sector agencies to place locals into PMET jobs in sectors with good growth potential.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: A key thrust under this initiative is to reskill locals through our Professional Conversion Programmes (PCP) to take up good job opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Locals comprise around 75% of employed PMETs in these growth sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Over the past three years, the Adapt and Grow initiative has helped more than 48,000 local jobseekers get placed in PMET roles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: As a result of more focused efforts under the Growth Sectors Initiative, Workforce Singapore and sector agencies have placed over 10,000 mid-career locals into PMET jobs in the growth sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Over nine in 10 PCP participants remained in employment two years after placement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Around seven in 10 PCP participants earned higher salaries than before.

sections.label: Local PMET numbers and share
sections.summary: Local PMETs grew from about 960,000 in 2009 to 1.3 million in 2019, with their share of employed locals rising from 51.4% to 58.3%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The number of local PMETs grew from about 960,000 in 2009 to 1.3 million in 2019, while the PMET share of employed locals increased steadily from 51.4% to 58.3% over the same period.
